about: English for each person of a French verb, as the Verb forms step shows it. {base} is the English verb (want), {s} its he/she form (wants), {ing} its -ing form (leaving). simple is the plain present; progressive is used when a lesson's conjugation says aspect progressive (I'm leaving). be lists the forms of to be, the one English verb whose persons differ.

simple.prs.2sg: you {base} (to one person you know well)
simple.prs.2pl: you {base} (polite, or to more than one)

progressive.prs.2sg: you're {ing} (to one person you know well)
progressive.prs.2pl: you're {ing} (polite, or to more than one)

be.prs.2sg: you are (to one person you know well)
be.prs.3sg: he is, she is, we are (on)
be.prs.2pl: you are (polite, or to more than one)
